    Home/Hair growth

    Peptides for hair loss, compared with the proven options.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Checked 2 Nov 2026.

    Every claim links to its source.

    Finasteride and minoxidil are the only treatments on this page the FDA has approved for hair loss, and generic finasteride starts at about $10 a month. Copper peptide serums are cosmetics: the evidence is from lab and follicle-culture studies, not from large trials in people.

    Is it legal today?

    For thinning hair, a receding hairline or bald spots: what slows the loss, what regrows hair, and what is only marketing.

    • Finasteride 1 mgFDA approvedProven alternativeFrom $25/mo at online clinics · 1 clinic1 FDA letter 20 Feb 2026

      A daily pill. Slows hair loss and regrows some hair in most men; not for women who may become pregnant.

      FDA approved for hair loss.

      Prescription, from an online clinic or your doctor. From $10/mo (generic, pharmacy coupon).3 Online clinics from $25/mo (Strut Health).1 FDA letter 20 Feb 2026

      Evidence in people: Strong: many trials in people · Needs a prescription

      See plans at Strut Health · $25/moOpens our clinic page
    • MinoxidilFDA approvedProven alternativeFrom $30/mo at online clinics · 1 clinic2

      A liquid or foam you put on the scalp twice a day. Regrows hair for men and women; works while you keep using it.

      FDA approved for hair loss.

      No prescription, any pharmacy. From $10/mo.4 Online clinics from $30/mo (Keeps).2

      Evidence in people: Strong: many trials in people · No prescription needed

      See plans at Keeps · $30/moPharmacy, no prescription
    • GHK-Cu copper peptide serumCosmetic, no approval needed

      A cosmetic serum for the scalp. Small lab and follicle studies; no large trials in people.

      Cosmetic: legal to sell, nobody checked that it works.

      Sold in shops, no prescription.

      Evidence in people: Limited: lab and follicle-culture studies · No prescription needed

      Sold as a cosmetic; prices come later.
    • Injectable peptides sold for hairNot approved for any useFrom $1.14/mg at 10 shops

      Vials from research-use shops, meant to be injected. No human evidence for hair.

      Not approved for any use.

      We do not link to them.

      Evidence in people: None found in people

    Is it legal today?

    FDA status checked 31 Oct 2026

    Injectable peptides sold for hair are not approved for any use, and we found no human evidence for hair.

    FDA status of the peptides on this page, each with its source.

    PeptideStatusWhat that means
    BPC-157Not approvedits nomination for pharmacy compounding was withdrawn FDA source, 19 Oct 2026. FDA advisory committee reviewed it for compounding on 23 Jul 2026; FDA proposed not to allow it. 5
    FinasterideFDA approvedan FDA-approved product exists for hair loss FDA source, 31 Oct 2026
    GHK-Cu (as a drug)Not approvedits nomination for pharmacy compounding was withdrawn FDA source, 19 Oct 2026
    GHK-Cu (cream or serum)Cosmeticcosmetics are regulated but do not need FDA approval to be sold 6
    MinoxidilFDA approvedan FDA-approved product exists for hair loss FDA source, 31 Oct 2026
    TB-500 (thymosin beta-4 fragment 17-23)Not approvedits nomination for pharmacy compounding was withdrawn FDA source, 19 Oct 2026. Same July 2026 review; FDA proposed not to allow it. 5

    Approved means the FDA approved a product containing it for a stated use. Not approved means no approved product exists; buying it for yourself is not a crime in the US, but nobody has checked what is in the vial. All substances
